5e9cb9311f81bf1ad9fcef04d32034119ebd1008.summary: Describes two new Monero cryptocurrency-mining malware attacks, one on Windows PCs and one on Android devices, both disguised as legitimate updates. The Windows infection, reported by Quick Heal Security Labs, unpacks scripts and a mining program, keeps itself persistent, caps mining CPU use at 35 percent and checks for analysis and antivirus tools. The Android malware HiddenMiner, reported by Fortinet, poses as a Google Play Store update, asks for administrator rights and shuts down in emulators. 5e0c595451085d5955884726970a4ce860178bca.summary: A code-hosting repository page advertising a tool that builds a Windows trojan. It describes keylogging, screen capture and remote command control. It is a tool listing, not an analysis of threat activity, so no threat facts are recorded.

5e48fa8ab017554c8a3407eaf6ae01823a4558ff.summary: TrendAI Research analysed a supply chain compromise in which trojanized npm packages sold as date-math utilities contain a loader that starts a Linux binary when the module loads. The binary is the RedShell Linux implant of the RedC2 4.0 framework, which the report says is marketed on Hack Forums. Described capabilities include shell access, SSH key and browser credential collection, database discovery, plaintext HTTP exfiltration, fileless execution, persistence and SOCKS5 pivoting.
